openQuestions.question: Is the wait for the next service the full headway, the average (half headway), or modelled from the mission clock?
openQuestions.why: The GDD says price = wait + ride from the timetable but does not define how the wait is computed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a walking pace, and does boarding count the interchange walk as part of the price?
openQuestions.why: The GDD states no walking pace; 1.4 m/s is an [S] assumption for interchange walks.

openQuestions.question: Can a boarded vehicle be seen, stopped or sealed (e.g. Alert 3 closing stations)?
openQuestions.why: The timetable assumes continuous service; the GDD travel rule does not cover closures.

openQuestions.question: Does the T2 ring run in both directions, and does a rider choose the shorter way round?
openQuestions.why: The GDD does not say; journeys here assume either direction on the line.

notes: T1 speed 8 m/s [S]: street tram on a 16 m street, stops 300-500 m apart; runs of ~310 m take ~39 s. Dwell 15 s, headway 180 s.
T2 speed 8 m/s [S]: street ring tram with the same street-running conditions as T1, runs of 310-460 m. Headway 240 s [S] because the ring is long (about 2.9 km chainage), dwell 15 s.
S1 speed 12 m/s [S]: elevated rail, faster than trams on 200-250 m spacing; headway 120 s, dwell 12 s. Speeds, dwells and headways for T1 and S1 are unchanged from the last round.
Three interchanges now exist: T1/circus-S1/circus, T1/comet-T2/comet, T2/harbour-S1/harbour, each within the 150 m limit. Interchange walks come from code.
Journeys cover every interchange, both directions, and two three-leg trips linking all three lines (Records to Skyport, Crescent to Records).
Boarding is fast travel priced in time only (wait + ride), no fare, per the GDD travel rule.
